description: Mechanical Engineering student interested in Robotics, Drones, Aerospace, and Mars exploration. Looking for team members skilled in coding, CAD, electronics, data analysis, and visualization to build an innovative Mars mission solution.
summary:
The Marswalk Planner is an interactive map of Jezero Crater that helps plan a human walk on Mars. It stacks seven layers on one grid: relief, geology, elevation, slope, temperature, hydration and rock cover. Time and season controls change the sun, shadows, temperature and dust. A route planner finds walkable paths around steep ground. Each route receives a Go, Caution or No-Go verdict based on walk-back range, slope, EVA time, daylight, cold, dust and radiation. Eight science targets and three hazards are marked.
The project answers the challenge with an integrated, layered view: tapping any point shows every value together. Each layer represents real products from NASA missions such as MRO, Odyssey, Curiosity and Perseverance. Ranked targets let a route be both safe and scientifically useful.
It matters because a crew far from base has little margin for error. The planner shows risks before anyone steps outside, tests whether a route fits time, light and oxygen limits, and balances valuable rocks against the cost of reaching them. With Mars Sample Return cancelled, cached samples remain on Mars, and a future crew could retrieve them. The terrain is currently modelled; real Mars Trek data is next.
details:
Marswalk Planner: complete project details
Team: MechFusion
Challenge: Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map (NASA Space Apps)
Date: 15 November 2026
One-line summary
An interactive map that combines NASA Mars data layers and turns them into a Go, Caution or No-Go decision for a human Marswalk in Jezero Crater.
Problem
A crew on Mars needs to know where it is safe to go, what is worth studying, whether they can walk back, and whether light and weather allow it. The data is scattered across many missions and formats.
Solution
One map where all layers sit on the same grid, tied to a route planner and a set of safety checks.
Study area
Jezero Crater, roughly 18.2 to 18.6°N and 77.15 to 77.65°E.
A window of about 28 × 24 km at 80 m per cell.
Start and finish at the Butler landing site.
Features
Seven layers: relief, geology, elevation, slope, temperature, hydration and rock cover, with adjustable opacity.
Time and season: a 24-hour clock and a season slider move the sun, shadows and temperatures. There is also a dust-storm toggle and a one-sol animation.
Routing: three presets or tap-to-add waypoints. Routes go around steep ground, are coloured by slope, and come with an elevation profile.
Checks: walk-back range (default 6.5 km), slope, EVA time (default 8 h), daylight, cold, dust and radiation.
Inspector: tap any point for position, elevation, slope, terrain, temperature, rock cover and sunlight.
Targets: eight science targets and three hazards, each with its data source.
Extras: a mission update card, five accent colours and light and dark modes.
NASA data the layers represent
Elevation and slope: MOLA, HRSC, CTX and HiRISE terrain models.
Imagery: CTX and HiRISE (MRO).
Temperature: THEMIS, TES and MEDA.
Minerals and hydration: CRISM.
Rocks: thermal-inertia maps and boulder counts.
Weather and dust: MARCI and MEDA.
Radiation: Curiosity's RAD.
Technology
Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file, with no outside libraries. Maps are drawn on canvas, and routing is a best-first search on an 8-connected grid.
Key assumptions
Suited walking speed is 3 km/h on level ground, adjusted for slope.
Cells steeper than 32° are blocked.
Rock adds up to 40% to walking time, and sand adds 15%.
Each science stop takes 20 minutes.
The checks apply the thresholds listed in the report.
Test results
Delta front: 15.5 km, 7.2 h EVA, Caution because of a steep ramp.
Séítah and Máaz: 12.3 km, 5.1 h EVA, Go.
Margin carbonates: 29.8 km, 10.8 h EVA, No-Go on foot.
Latest mission context (15 Nov 2026)
Perseverance is on sol 2033 and has driven about 45.25 km.
It has filled about 30 of 38 sample tubes.
It is working just west of the crater rim.
NASA reported complex organic carbon in the Bright Angel sample.
Mars Sample Return was cancelled, so cached samples stay on Mars for now.
Impact
Safety: risks are visible before a crew steps outside.
Efficiency: routes are tested against time, light and oxygen limits.
Science: valuable targets are weighed against their cost.
Usability: scattered data becomes one decision view.
Limitations
The terrain values are our own stylised model, not downloaded NASA data, and feature positions are approximate.
The thresholds are assumptions.
Nothing was compared with real measurements.
Radio line of sight, power and consumables are not modelled.
Mission facts come from news reports of NASA updates, so check NASA and JPL pages before quoting.
Future work
Load real Mars Trek elevation and imagery.
Extend the map west to the rim.
Validate routes against Perseverance's real drives.
Add communications, power and consumables limits.
Compare walking with a pressurised rover.
